skill.name: prisma-next-queries
skill.description: Write target-aware Prisma Next queries for Postgres, SQLite, and Mongo using typed ORM, SQL builder, pipeline, relation, aggregation, pagination, and transaction patterns.
skill.summary: Create correct Prisma Next reads, writes, relations, aggregates, and transactions for each supported database target.
skill.author: prisma

content.user_title: Write Prisma Next Queries Across Database Targets
content.value_statement: Prisma Next query APIs differ across Postgres, SQLite, and Mongo, which makes correct lane selection difficult. This skill provides target-specific patterns for typed reads, writes, relations, aggregates, pagination, and transactions.
actual_capabilities: Selects the correct ORM or lower-level query lane for Postgres, SQLite, and Mongo.
Builds typed CRUD queries with filters, projections, sorting, and pagination.
Explains eager loading, namespace-aware accessors, and polymorphic Mongo roots.
Creates Postgres aggregates, SQL-builder plans, and transactional workflows.
Creates Mongo aggregation pipelines, lookups, and filtered write plans.
Handles Thenable query results, streaming iteration, and short-script teardown.
limitations: It does not define data contracts, configure runtime bindings, or diagnose structured query failures.
Prisma Next currently lacks raw SQL, TypedSQL, query-plan inspection, and built-in result streaming.
The Mongo facade does not provide transactions or ORM aggregate methods.
Many-to-many includes and nested many-to-many mutations are not fully supported.

use_cases.title: Build application queries
use_cases.description: Create typed reads, writes, relation includes, and pagination for an application service.

use_cases.title: Create database analytics
use_cases.description: Build Postgres aggregates or Mongo pipelines with grouping, projection, and joins.

use_cases.title: Translate query styles
use_cases.description: Convert familiar Prisma, Drizzle, or Kysely patterns into supported Prisma Next APIs.

prompt_templates.title: Write a basic query
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Prisma Next query for [target] that returns [records] filtered by [condition].

prompt_templates.title: Add relations and pagination
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [target] query for [model] with [relation], selected fields, stable sorting, and [page size] results.

prompt_templates.title: Build an aggregate
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Prisma Next [Postgres or Mongo] aggregation that groups by [field] and calculates [metrics].

prompt_templates.title: Design an atomic workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Prisma Next workflow for [operations], using transactions where supported and explaining target limitations.

output_examples.input: Fetch the newest posts with authors from a Postgres project.
output_examples.output: Uses the Postgres ORM, includes the author relation, applies descending creation order, limits results, and awaits the collection once.

output_examples.input: Count Mongo posts by category for one author.
output_examples.output: Uses the Mongo query builder with an author match, category grouping, count accumulator, plan construction, and runtime execution.

output_examples.input: Create a user and post atomically.
output_examples.output: Uses one Postgres transaction and its shared context, while noting that the Mongo facade does not support this transaction workflow.

best_practices: Confirm the runtime target before choosing model names, filters, or query lanes.
Use the ORM for standard CRUD and relations, then use builders for unsupported shapes.
Apply filters to mutations and consume each asynchronous result only once.
anti_patterns: Do not mix Postgres model accessors with Mongo collection accessors.
Do not use unrestricted reads when a single-row method or bounded page is required.
Do not invent raw SQL, Mongo transactions, or ORM aggregate APIs that are unavailable.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Prisma Next query patterns for Postgres, SQLite, and Mongo.

faq.question: Does it generate data contracts?
faq.answer: No. Use the Prisma Next contract workflow to create or change models.

faq.question: When should I use the ORM?
faq.answer: Use the ORM for standard CRUD, filtering, projection, pagination, and relation loading.

faq.question: When should I use a lower-level builder?
faq.answer: Use it for explicit joins, computed projections, Mongo pipelines, or other shapes the ORM cannot express.

faq.question: Does Mongo support transactions through this facade?
faq.answer: No. The current Mongo facade requires direct driver sessions for multi-document transactions.

faq.question: How should I consume all query results?
faq.answer: Await the result directly for an array, or iterate once when incremental processing is needed.
